items.title: Easy walk
items.summary: A relaxed walk at a pace where you can still chat.
steps: Start by walking slowly for a minute.
Settle into a comfortable pace and keep your shoulders loose.
Walk for as long as feels good, then slow down for the last minute.
items.safetyNote: Stop if anything hurts or feels wrong. This is general wellbeing information, not medical advice; check with a health professional if you have a condition, are pregnant or are unsure.

items.title: Morning wake-up stretch
items.summary: A few slow stretches to start the day.
steps: Stand tall and roll your shoulders back five times.
Reach both arms overhead and take two slow breaths.
Gently tilt your head to one side, then the other, without forcing.
Sway your hips side to side for a few breaths.
items.safetyNote: Stop if anything hurts or feels wrong. This is general wellbeing information, not medical advice; check with a health professional if you have a condition, are pregnant or are unsure.

items.title: Desk break: neck and shoulders
steps: Sit tall with your feet flat.
Lift your shoulders toward your ears, then let them drop, five times.
Turn your head slowly to look over each shoulder.
items.safetyNote: Stop if anything hurts or feels wrong. This is general wellbeing information, not medical advice; check with a health professional if you have a condition, are pregnant or are unsure.

items.title: Evening unwind stretches
items.summary: A short, slow stretching routine for the end of the day.
steps: Sit on the floor or a bed with your legs out and reach gently toward your toes.
Lie on your back and hug one knee to your chest, then the other.
Let both knees fall to one side for a gentle twist, then switch.
Finish lying still for five slow breaths.
items.safetyNote: Stop if anything hurts or feels wrong. This is general wellbeing information, not medical advice; check with a health professional if you have a condition, are pregnant or are unsure.

items.title: Bodyweight basics
items.summary: A simple beginner circuit using your own weight.
steps: March on the spot for one minute to warm up.
Do 8–10 chair sits (stand up from a chair and sit back down slowly).
Do 8–10 wall push-ups.
Rest as long as you like, then repeat once if it feels good.
items.safetyNote: Stop if anything hurts or feels wrong. This is general wellbeing information, not medical advice; check with a health professional if you have a condition, are pregnant or are unsure.

items.title: Three calm breaths
steps: Sit or stand comfortably and relax your shoulders.
Breathe in through your nose for a count of four.
Breathe out slowly for a count of six. Repeat for three breaths.

items.title: Paced breathing
items.summary: A few minutes of slow, even breathing.
steps: Get comfortable and soften your jaw.
Breathe in for four counts and out for four counts.
If your mind wanders, gently return to counting. Continue for three minutes.

items.title: Short body scan
items.summary: A five-minute check-in from head to toe.
steps: Lie down or sit and close your eyes if you like.
Bring attention to your forehead, then slowly move down: face, neck, shoulders, arms, belly, legs, feet.
At each place, notice how it feels without trying to change it.
Finish with a slow breath and open your eyes.

items.title: Warm foot soak
items.summary: A quiet evening ritual for tired feet.
steps: Fill a basin with comfortably warm water; test it with your hand first.
Sit with your feet in the water for 10–15 minutes.
Dry your feet well and, if you like, rub in a little moisturiser.
items.safetyNote: Stop if anything hurts or feels wrong. This is general wellbeing information, not medical advice; check with a health professional if you have a condition, are pregnant or are unsure.

items.title: Gentle facial massage
items.summary: A slow, light-touch moment for yourself.
steps: Wash your hands and apply a little of your usual face oil or cream.
With your fingertips, stroke lightly from the centre of your face outward.
Keep the pressure light and stop if your skin feels irritated.
equipment: Your usual face oil or cream
items.safetyNote: Stop if anything hurts or feels wrong. This is general wellbeing information, not medical advice; check with a health professional if you have a condition, are pregnant or are unsure.

items.title: Mindful tea break
items.summary: Five minutes with a warm drink and nothing else.
steps: Make a cup of tea you enjoy.
Sit somewhere comfortable, phone away.
Notice the warmth of the cup, the smell and each sip.

items.title: Relaxing evening routine
items.summary: A simple sequence to close the day.
steps: Dim the lights and put screens away for a while.
Have a warm drink and do the evening unwind stretches.
Write down one thing from the day you are glad about.

items.title: Simple grounding
items.summary: A short pause using your senses.
steps: Stand or sit and feel your feet on the floor.
Name five things you can see, four you can feel, three you can hear.
Take a slow breath out.
